title: A finitely generated separable field extension is the fraction field of a smooth algebra
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$) which is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Then there is a $k$-subalgebra $B\subseteq K$ such that $k\to B$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $K$ is the fraction field of $B$, i.e. every element of $K$ is $b/b'$ with $b,b'\in B$, $b'\neq0$ (so $B$ is a domain and $B\to K$ is a localization of $B$ at $B\setminus\{0\}$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 037X (lemma-localization-smooth-separable, line 44512), implication 'separable => localization of a smooth k-algebra', in the form used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0381 ('there exists a smooth k'-algebra B such that K' is the fraction field of B'); its proof: choose a finite type domain R with fraction field K and apply Lemma Tag 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point): k -> R is smooth at (0), so R_g is smooth for some g != 0 (Definition Tag 00TB definition-smooth-at-prime)

proof.text: (A domain of finite type with fraction field $K$.) Write $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ and let $R=k[a_1,\dots,a_n]\subseteq K$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by $a_1,\dots,a_n$, i.e. the image of the $k$-algebra map $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to K$, $x_i\mapsto a_i$; so $R\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ ($\mathfrak a$ the kernel) is a $k$-algebra of finite type, and $R$ is a domain, being a subring of the field $K$. The set $F=\{b/b':b,b'\in R,\ b'\neq0\}\subseteq K$ is closed under sums, products and inverses of nonzero elements, so it is a subfield of $K$; it contains $k$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n$, hence $F=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)=K$. Thus $K$ is the fraction field of $R$, and the field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] is the one given by $k\to R\subseteq K$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 037X (lemma-localization-smooth-separable, line 44512): 'Choose a finite type k-algebra R which is a domain whose fraction field is K'

proof.text: (Smooth at the generic point.) $R$ is a $k$-algebra of finite type which is a domain, its fraction field is $K$ (Step 1), and $K/k$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-generic-point-over-field] the ring map $k\to R$ is smooth at the prime $(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in R$, $g\neq0$, such that the localization $R_g$ of $R$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 037X (line 44512): 'Lemma 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point) says that k -> R is smooth at (0) if and only if K/k is separable'; smooth at a prime: Definition Tag 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime, line 37511)

proof.text: (The subalgebra $B$.) Since $g\neq0$ in the field $K$, $g$ is invertible in $K$; let $B=R[g^{-1}]=\{r g^{-m}:r\in R,\ m\ge0\}\subseteq K$, the $k$-subalgebra of $K$ generated by $R$ and $g^{-1}$. The $k$-algebra map $R_g\to K$, $r/g^m\mapsto rg^{-m}$, is well defined (by the universal property of $R_g$, as $g$ is a unit of $K$), has image $B$, and is injective: if $rg^{-m}=0$ in $K$ then $r=0$, so $r/g^m=0$. Hence $R_g\cong B$ as $k$-algebras, and $k\to B$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] by Step 2, each of the three conditions of smoothness (finite presentation, $H_1(L_{B/k})=0$, $\Omega_{B/k}$ finite projective) being carried along a $k$-algebra isomorphism. Finally $R\subseteq B\subseteq K$ and every element of $K$ is $b/b'$ with $b,b'\in R\subseteq B$, $b'\neq0$ (Step 1), so $K$ is the fraction field of $B$; in particular $B$ is a domain, every element of $B\setminus\{0\}$ is invertible in $K$, and $B\to K$ is a localization of $B$ at $B\setminus\{0\}$.
